newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra chief says Losec has more to give.
newsitem.headline: Astra chief says Losec has more to give.

text.p: Swedish drugmaker Astra said on Monday its blockbusting ulcer drug Losec had plenty more to give on the U.S. market, and that other products in the R&D pipeline would take over where Losec leaves off.

"Losec has not been on the U.S. market very long, the growth rate there is around 40 percent, so we still have more potential there," Astra president Hakan Mogren told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) in an interview.
Broader approvals for use of the drug in Japan in late 1997 or early 1998 would also help keep up the momentum of Losec sales, Mogren said.
One key area for expansion on the sales side would be existing products dosed in Astra's Turbuhaler inhaler form, Mogren said.
He said the company's considerable cash assets could be used in a variety of different ways, in which research and development could be one.
"As long as we have good projects we should do our best in R&D and we did increase speed there.
"Our ambition is to continue growing from this (R&D) base by around 20 percent per year in expenditure terms. If we see more opportunities then we'll add something more to that," Mogren said.
